about: scripts/servercount and benchmarks/server/registry (wf10 N2 SERVER-COUNT): the driver's replay must check an answer for every exchange and compare each body's digest, and the registry's three sides (the Ergo program, control/ and floor/) must answer as the model in registry.go. The replay rows are killed by the in-process tests; the sides rows by TestSidesAnswerAsTheModel (full tier: it builds the three servers); the program's own rows also by its laws, run with ergo test (command registry-laws).

mutants.name: servercount-status-only
mutants.rule: A run counts an answer only after comparing its status and its body's digest with the script's: a wrong answer voids the run.

mutants.name: servercount-replay-drops-a-connection
mutants.rule: A run sends every exchange of its script, on every connection, and checks each answer.

mutants.name: servercount-control-listing-order
mutants.rule: The control lists the catalog as the program does, in name order: the receipt compares sides that send the same bytes.

mutants.name: servercount-floor-no-body-limit
mutants.rule: The floor keeps the program's limits: a body over maxBody is refused with 413, never read as a pin.

mutants.name: registry-hook-unsigned
mutants.rule: A hook is taken only under its body's signature (api.ergo, AgreesWithModel).

mutants.name: registry-find-longer-name
mutants.rule: A package is found under its own name only (catalog.ergo, FindsEachName); no script sends a longer name, so no other test sees it.
